faqs.question: Do I need a thermal printer?
faqs.answer: No. The editor works entirely in the browser. Printing currently needs an Epson TM-L90 on 80 or 58 mm paper and the small local bridge running on your machine.

faqs.question: What is WebMCP?
faqs.answer: WebMCP lets a web page expose its tools to AI agents. A compatible agent can read the receipt, draft and edit blocks, preview the print, and ask for approval — the same operations you have in the editor.

faqs.question: Can an agent print by itself?
faqs.answer: It can request a print, but every job waits for your approval, bound to the exact revision you reviewed. Any edit you make cancels a pending request.

faqs.question: Does anything leave my machine?
faqs.answer: Your receipts, settings, and print jobs stay on this machine. Blocks like weather or news fetch public APIs only when you add them, and say so.

faqs.question: Is OpenReceipt free?
faqs.answer: Yes. OpenReceipt is MIT-licensed software that currently runs from source on the machine beside the printer.

faqs.question: Which printers are supported?
faqs.answer: OpenReceipt currently ships one physically tested adapter: the Epson TM-L90 over native USB, with 80 mm (576-dot) and 58 mm (420-dot) paper profiles. The workshop explains other ESC/POS paths without claiming they work in this app.
